rules.description: Validated-but-stale: armed (ai_validating) + validation concluded but BASE MOVED (BEHIND only). BLOCKED must NOT unarm: since #483 BLOCKED is a real verdict, and on a freshly armed head BLOCKED simply means 'required checks pending' — unarming there races validate-armed in the SAME tick and deadlocks the PR forever (live: fa pr-762 armed at 08:25:37, unarmed 08:25:58 by the BLOCKED match, re-armed next tick, loop). silent-update-behind excludes ai_validating and merge-validated needs CLEAN, so without this unarm a genuinely moved base still deadlocks (live: fa pr-744) — BEHIND-only keeps that recovery and stops the self-inflicted one.

Stale-arm sweeper (live: fa #999 — ai_validating held 7h with a CONCLUDED green CI and no verdict consumed; the ai_validating mutex stayed held forever. unarm-stale-validation covers BEHIND only). ai_validating + the head's dispatched validation run CONCLUDED (success or failure — CANCELLED is never a verdict) more than staleMinutes (15) ago, arm never consumed → unarm. Success side: unarm + re-latch ai_validated (complete_validation parity — the merge window re-flows; validate-armed latch-skips on the unchanged head). Failure side: the standard fail path (report + machine-only rework re-arm). Fresh conclusions (<15 min) never sweep: the check-visibility/verdict race window — the same-tick verdict rules (merge-validated / fail-validation / validated-green) own those. BEHIND excluded: unarm-stale-validation owns the moved-base recovery.

Every open non-draft PR behind main gets a silent branch refresh with the workflow token (pushes trigger no workflows, so freshness is free); validating PRs are excluded so the validation head never moves mid-run. mergeState is BEHIND only: the prStatus deterministic override computes BEHIND from base freshness (immune to the REST BEHIND/BLOCKED flip-flop this rule used to paper over with both values), and BLOCKED is now a REAL verdict (fresh head, required checks pending/red) — updating those would no-op-clone every pending PR on every tick. Limit 20 (owner 2026-09-22): silent pushes fire no CI — refreshing every BEHIND head every tick is free and keeps PRs merge-ready, so the merge window never waits for a refresh first. STICKY PARK (owner 2026-09-27, live: fa#923): before refreshing, a GUEST PR whose current head has RED checks is labeled validation_failed (idempotent, the head SHA noted in a one-time comment) — validate-armed excludes the label and no validation CI is dispatched for it at all; the label is REMOVED only when the head's LAST committer is NOT 'sm-silent-update' (an author push), so the SM's own silent-updates never re-arm a red guest. Machine-authored PRs never get the label (fa pushes their heads).

Post-approval merge window — OWNER FIFO RULE (2026-09-22): lead the OLDEST approved PR all the way to merge; never validate other approved PRs meanwhile (the merge moves the base — they would re-validate anyway). Advance to the next approved ONLY when the oldest is DIRTY (conflict-rework owns it) or its validation went RED (rework leg fixes it) — both free this slot while the oldest repairs. BEHIND/DIRTY excluded here: silent-update refreshes BEHIND heads first; conflicted heads can never reach CLEAN. Mutex ai_validating = one validation at a time. validation_failed excluded (owner 2026-09-27, live: fa#923 — a GUEST PR whose head went red cycles arm→CI red→silent-update→re-arm forever, holding this limit-1 slot hostage; the silent-update action labels such guests validation_failed and they stay parked until a NON-MACHINE push moves the head).

Armed head moved mid-validation (double silent-update, rework push): the green run no longer covers the head, checks read 'none' on it, but the ai_validating arm persists — no rule matched and the PR stalled until a manual disarm (live: dart pr-194, 15:06 — tick processed 0). Re-dispatch the CI on the CURRENT head. 'pending' never matches: that is the in-flight bridge check on this head. BEHIND/DIRTY excluded like validate-armed. MUTEX with mutexExcludeSelf (multi-arm leak fix, live: fa 2026-09-26 — 7 approved PRs held ai_validating simultaneously: 922/923/930/932/934/948/961, +1 arm per tick): this rule previously ran with NO mutex because the global mutex scan sees the rule's own armed target and self-blocks 100% of the time — and its 'structural serialization' assumption (validate-armed's mutex guarantees <=1 armed approved PR) is FALSE once heads move: silent-update / BEHIND unarm races / guest pushes keep feeding checks=none states, and each tick this rule armed one more approved PR. The exclude-self mutex (githubSource) evaluates per candidate: it defers only while ANOTHER approved PR holds ai_validating. Exactly one armed approved PR = the candidate itself = the rule fires; a second approved arm anywhere = every candidate defers and the stack drains via merge-validated / fail-validation / unarm-stale.

Dead-zone fix (live: fa pr-922, 2026-09-26 — frozen in ai_validating for hours, ticks processed 0): the armed head's dispatched CI run was LOST (racing dispatch canceled by concurrency, or the gh workflow run CLI call failed silently — dispatchCiWorkflow cannot throw). Every existing check is green, but the required CI check is ABSENT from the head, so the rollup reads 'green' while REST mergeState stays BLOCKED. No rule matched: revalidate-armed wants checks=none, merge-validated wants CLEAN, fail-validation wants red, unarm-stale wants BEHIND. 'green' + not-CLEAN here means the arm is stale and the CI verdict is missing — re-dispatch (validate_pr's duplicate-dispatch guard skips if a run is already landing; the skipIfGreenCi flag stops the loop when a completed green CI run already covers the head and the blocker is some other workflow's required check). Armed+green+CLEAN must NOT match — that is merge-validated's merge — hence CLEAN is excluded. MUTEX with mutexExcludeSelf (multi-arm leak fix, live: fa 2026-09-26 — 7 approved PRs armed at once): same self-block reason as revalidate-armed made this rule ship mutex-less, and the same false singleton assumption let it feed the +1-arm-per-tick leak. The exclude-self mutex defers the candidate only while ANOTHER approved PR holds ai_validating; with the invariant restored this rule fires exactly on the one armed approved PR and never arms a second.

GitHub PR: head with no CONCLUDED validation (checks 'none' — fresh push, no CI — or 'pending' — the dispatch bridge's waiting check runs; pushes fire no CI) -> dispatch the CI workflow on the head + ai_validating marker. OWNER RULE (2026-09-23, validation economy): validate ONCE per PR — the first green is the ticket to review; after it the ai_validated latch excludes the PR here, silent-update keeps it fresh (no re-validation on refresh), and the single pre-merge validation lives in validate-armed (post-approve, current head). Red heads repeat this rule only after a NEW push clears the red. chore:pin PRs (factory lockstep bumps) are exempt: the factory suite gates them before the cut, and the next real PR validates the pinned content via silent-update.

GitHub PR: validation CI red on the head -> unarm ai_validating, report, requeue agent:rework on the linked issue. pr_approved is STICKY (owner rule 2026-09): the reworked head re-validates and merges without a re-review — no token burn on review legs. Limit 10 (owner 2026-09-22): latch/unlatch verdicts in waves — pure label writes, nothing serial.

GitHub PR: validation green + CLEAN -> squash-merge (merge_pr verifies the sticky pr_approved latch on the PR; an un-approved green head latches ai_validated instead — see merge_pr). FIFO drain (#687).

GitHub PR: validation green but not yet approved -> latch ai_validated, unarm ai_validating. review-after-dev requires the latch + green checks, so review fires exactly once per validated head. Approved PRs are excluded (merge-validated / unarm-stale own them). Limit 10 (owner 2026-09-22): latch/unlatch verdicts in waves — pure label writes, nothing serial.

GitHub PR: branch conflicts with main (silent-update's git merge cannot land; mergeState DIRTY) -> the queue would stall forever — report and, for MACHINE-authored PRs, re-arm agent:rework on the linked issue so the agent resolves the conflicts and pushes; the normal validate flow then resumes (pr_approved is STICKY — no re-review). Guest PRs get the report only (owner rule 2026-09-21: auto-rework is machine-author-only). Fires once per head: the marker comment carries the head sha and suppresses re-reports for the same head.

Auto rework leg: agent:rework armed on the issue either by the review verdict (CHANGES_REQUESTED) or by red pre-merge CI. Pushing fixes removes the label (pr_rework removeLabels). prMachineAuthor: auto rework fires ONLY on machine-authored PRs (owner rule) — the machine login is deployment config (jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor / factory-sm machine-author input), never hardcoded; unconfigured fails closed. Manual rework on ANY PR: label the PR agent:rework (see rework-on-label). workflowRef={branch}: the leg runs on the PR head — GitHub links the run to the PR (visible in PR checks/timeline as the review/rework run).

inputs.reason: sm: agent:rework (red CI or review CHANGES)

rules.description: Manual rework request: agent:rework label on the PR itself -> rework on demand, ANY author (owner override: a manual label by a write/admin actor fires even on guest PRs). Dispatches the issue-anchored rework leg on the linked issue when the scrape resolves to an EXISTING LOCAL issue (verified via github_get_issue); when the PR has no valid local issue (cross-repo/dangling ref, issue-less PR) falls back to a PR-anchored rework dispatch (inputs.pr, guard runs the rework leg on pr-<N>) instead of crashing (#544). The PR label is consumed on dispatch so the next tick does not re-fire. workflowRef={branch}: the leg runs on the PR head.

inputs.reason: sm: agent:rework label on the PR (manual rework request)

rules.description: Machine-loop completion backfill: an open issue with an open+green MACHINE-authored PR gets ai_developed, which arms review-after-dev. Machine-only (prMachineAuthor) so external PRs never enter the review loop through the backfill; no `in progress` requirement — issues whose dev leg predates the status-label convention (live: fa #503 / PR #676) must still be picked up. Idempotent: ai_developed in notLabels.

GitHub: validated PR (ai_validated latch) after dev -> machine review (never on an armed PR: pr_approved means the review already concluded APPROVED - re-dispatching review duplicates the leg and un-arms the merge queue). OWNER RULE (2026-09-23, validation economy): the latch alone qualifies — no prChecks green requirement. silent-update keeps the head fresh; the review covers the current diff; the FINAL head gets its one pre-merge validation in validate-armed, so a head that moved since the latch's green is safe to review without re-running CI first. Limit 10 (owner 2026-09-22): review legs are plain workflow runs — they parallelize freely; one-per-tick serialized a 12-PR green wave into hours. workflowRef={branch}: the leg runs on the PR head — GitHub links the run to the PR (visible in PR checks/timeline as the review/rework run).

GitHub PR: external (non-machine) green PR -> one-time review (PR-anchored; no re-review on later pushes). The machine login is deployment-specific: it arrives via jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (factory-sm input machine-author); with none configured every green PR is reviewable.

inputs.reason: sm: external PR green - one-time review

rules.description: GitHub PR: MACHINE-authored validated PR whose review loop has no leg — the branch/body carry no OPEN linked issue (fix/*, revert/*, chore/* branches), or the linked issue closed: develop-done only backfills OPEN issues, review-after-dev rides the issue carrier, and review-external-once excludes machine authors — so such a PR starves validated-but-never-reviewed forever (live: fa #1068 validated 19h with zero review legs; #1071/#1075 in the same state, owner order 2026-09-30). PR-anchored one-time review, the machine-author twin of review-external-once. NO checks requirement (review-after-dev economy: the ai_validated latch alone qualifies — silent-update keeps the head fresh, the review covers the current diff, and the final pre-merge validation stays in validate-armed post-approve): a green-gated guard would skip silent-updated heads whose rollup reads 'none' (the exact skip that starved the trio). Dedup is structural, not green-gated: the leg runs on the PR head (workflowRef={branch}) so its check run flips the rollup to 'pending' — excluded here — until the runner latches ai_pr_reviewed at the verdict. prMachineAuthor fails CLOSED when no machineAuthor is configured (no auto legs at all). DIRTY heads are NOT excluded: a conflicted unlinked machine PR has no other path to a verdict (conflict-rework's rework re-arm needs the linked issue), and the merge window keeps it out of merges until CLEAN regardless. limit 1: same pacing as review-external-once; the trio drains over consecutive ticks.

inputs.reason: sm: machine PR validated but issue loop never armed a review - one-time review

rules.description: GitHub PR: CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict pinned to an older commit (fixes pushed after the review) + green -> re-arm agent:review. review-on-label dispatches the runner, the runner consumes the label and re-reviews the current head; the fresh verdict's commit_id equals the head, so this never loops. Never on approved PRs (pr_approved is sticky — approved rework re-validates, never re-reviews). workflowRef={branch}: the leg runs on the PR head — GitHub links the run to the PR (visible in PR checks/timeline as the review/rework run).

GitHub PR: all review threads resolved + the last verdict is older than the head (fixes landed and the threads were worked through) + green -> re-arm agent:review. Covers PR #676: the rework resolves threads (the CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict dissolves into COMMENTED), so verdict-staleness alone misses it. Convergent: the re-review's verdict lands on the current head and its fresh threads are unresolved until worked. Never on approved PRs (pr_approved is sticky — approved rework re-validates, never re-reviews). workflowRef={branch}: the leg runs on the PR head — GitHub links the run to the PR (visible in PR checks/timeline as the review/rework run).

GitHub PR: validated + reviewed (both latches) + ANY verdict pinned to an older commit + all review threads worked + the head has NO concluded checks (a push moved it after the review — silent-update/rework — so the rollup reads 'none' and every green-gated review path skips) -> RE-REVIEW FIRST (owner 2026-09-29: after ai_validated + a review, a moved head re-runs the REVIEW, never the validation; the single pre-merge validation stays in validate-armed, post-approve, on the final head). Closes the chicken-and-egg stall (live: fa pr-1076 + pr-1075, 2026-09-29 — a machine-authored PR whose head moved after its review stalled until a human label/manual dispatch, tick processed 0). checks 'none' ONLY: 'pending' is the in-flight dispatch bridge — racing it double-dispatches. threadsResolved excludes the mid-rework window (the rework leg owns open threads; its push flips them to resolved and arms THIS rule). Convergent: the fresh verdict's commit_id equals the head, so staleVerdict clears — never loops. Never on approved PRs (pr_approved is sticky — approved rework re-validates, never re-reviews). workflowRef={branch}: the leg runs on the PR head.

GitHub PR: agent:review label on a PR -> review on demand (any author; consumed by the review runner) workflowRef={branch}: the leg runs on the PR head — GitHub links the run to the PR (visible in PR checks/timeline as the review/rework run).
GitHub: linked PR merged → close the issue (cycle complete)
